title: Your UX portfolio, case study and 90-day plan

say: Your UX portfolio, case study and 90-day plan.
This is the video for module 4 of UX Design Fundamentals.
You already have the pieces of a real UX project: interviews, a persona, a flow, wireframes, a review and test results.
First you bring them together in one research pack, with participant codes, never names.

say: For example, Blessing's final salon prototype has 6 screens, including a slot just taken screen and a payment failure screen. She retests with 3 customers, and all 3 complete the booking.
Her research pack is a 14-page PDF with a link to the prototype.
Before you submit, check these five points, and open your share link on someone else's phone to make sure it works.

panel.heading: Blessing's final quality check
items: Main task works end to end
Error and empty states included
Contrast passes 4.5:1
Labels on every field
Consistent components used

say: Employers look for how you think, not just finished screens. Start with who struggled with what, then say what you did yourself and your limits, such as budget, devices or data.

panel.heading: The five parts of a case study
items: The problem and the users
Your role and your limits
Research and the top themes
Design, and what changed after testing
Results and what you would do next

say: Share your top 2 or 3 themes with a short quote. Then show one before and after, because side-by-side comparisons backed by test numbers convince people most.

say: End with your real numbers and an honest reflection.
You will tailor the opening for each reader, but the evidence never changes.

panel.rule: Keep the facts the same. Change only what you lead with.

say: Blessing writes three openings. For a design agency job, she leads with her research methods and her iterations.

cards.d: Lead with process: six interviews, two test rounds, success up from 3 of 5 to 5 of 5.
Lead with business: booking time cut from about 95 to about 48 seconds.
Lead with who is helped: tested with older customers and first-time smartphone users.

say: For the salon owner, she leads with customers: shorter booking time, and every tester booked without help.

say: For a women's business network, she leads with inclusion and who benefits.

say: Use your exact test numbers and say how many people took part. A practice project can say, concept project, tested with 8 participants. Employers respect that.

panel.heading: Honest results build trust
left: Say what you did not test
Say concept project if not launched
right: Post work a client kept private

say: Never show someone else's work as yours, and ask a client before showing their work publicly.
Saying, my price layout confused four of five people, so I changed it, shows strength, not weakness.

say: For example, Halima is a mother of two in Abuja with about 6 hours a week. She splits 90 days into three 30-day blocks, each with one goal and a number to check.
First, a second project tested with 5 users.

panel.heading: Halima's 90-day plan
items: Days 1 to 30: a second tested case study
Days 31 to 60: one real business and a testimonial
Days 61 to 90: first paid project with a scope
Every Friday: a 15-minute review

say: Next, she offers a low-cost heuristic review to 2 local businesses each week, until one agrees and gives a written testimonial.

panel.heading: Halima's 90-day plan

say: Then her first paid project. Beware offers that ask you to pay for a guaranteed job. Real clients agree a written scope first, and Halima takes a deposit by bank transfer or a Paystack payment link.

say: Every Friday she spends 15 minutes ticking off actions. Plan for the hours you really have, not the hours you wish you had.

say: To remember. Show your evidence. Polish only what has been tested. Tell a clear, honest story for each reader. To earn your certificate, complete the capstone and score at least 70 percent in the final quiz.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A research pack shows the evidence behind decisions
Visual design only after the structure is tested
Problem, role, research, design, results
Same facts, different openings for each reader
Score at least 70 percent in the final quiz
